grants.note: An AI agent may propose, amend, check and report evidence anywhere in HashRelay, through a Host delegation the owner mints. It may never accept, reject, revoke or supersede.

policy.note: Who may decide what about HashRelay, ENFORCED BY THE HOST (Vision V3 Stage 9; ADR-0010 in continuum-architecture). This document travels once, as the body of the space's genesis act; after that the policy IS the record's `governed` lines, and changing it is itself a `govern` act. A principal is an issuer + oid the Host verifies from a token. A workload grant (actingAs agent:…) is usable only through a delegation token the Host issues to that workload, and never exceeds the grant it is delegatedBy.

rules.note: A HashRelay decision is approved by a person, never by whoever proposed or amended it.

alternatives: Retain until acknowledged, with no bound (what the model says today): storage grows without limit for endpoints that never return
A per-workspace replay window: more configuration than any current workspace needs

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

consequences: Queued deliveries expire on a schedule, not only when the endpoint reconnects
Activity, duplicate and notification views stop counting expired deliveries as delivered
body.decision: A delivery queued for an offline endpoint is retained until it is acknowledged or until its replay window (ReplayWindowHours, 24 by default) elapses, whichever comes first. An expired delivery is recorded as expired and is never counted as delivered.

consequences.method: Host model.apply of the option's change to the decision's model

options.name: bounded-replay-window
options.summary: A delivery held for an offline endpoint is kept for a bounded replay window, after which it expires whether or not the endpoint returns; an expired delivery is reported as expired and never as delivered.

body.rationale: The model says queued deliveries are 'retained until acknowledged', but the code expires them after ReplayWindowHours, and only when the endpoint reconnects (RoutingService.ReplayAsync). Expired deliveries are then counted as delivered in RecentAsync, DuplicateAsync, the notification page and the dashboard. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lists offline retention as unresolved. Unbounded retention has no upper limit on storage for a device that never returns, so the bound is made explicit and the reporting is made honest.
risks: A device offline for longer than the window loses those notifications; it is told they expired, not that they were delivered
body.title: Offline deliveries are kept for a bounded replay window

alternatives: A Windows service that renders notifications: cannot reach the user session from session 0
A per-machine MSI install: needs admin rights and does not map an install to one user
Framework-dependent build: requires a matching .NET runtime on every machine

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

consequences: Notifications appear only while the user is signed in and the agent is running
Each Windows user who wants notifications installs and pairs their own agent
body.decision: On desktop, notifications are displayed only by DesktopAgent running in the signed-in user's session, through the platform notification center (on Windows, the Windows App SDK AppNotificationManager). No service, session-0 or server process renders user notifications. The Windows agent ships as a self-contained x64 build in a per-user Inno Setup installer that needs no admin rights.
body.rationale: Windows services run in session 0 and cannot show notifications in a user's session; native toasts need a process in that session with its own app identity. A per-user install keeps the agent with the user who paired it and avoids elevation. Recorded originally as docs/adr/0001-windows-first.md (2026-10-31), outside the decision record; this brings it in, without its offline-delivery clause, which ADR-001 replaces.
risks: A self-contained build is large and must be re-shipped for every .NET security patch
body.title: Native notifications are shown only by a per-user desktop agent
